rule_name: Undercut the Achievement in the Same Breath
why: the achievement is stated with its own full scene (blow-by-blow fight, lines 43-89) and the deflating rank ("you could have done that at thirteen," "having a gun isn't a skill") is withheld for a separate scene after a break, letting the reader marvel independently instead of the two facts landing joined in one breath as the rule requires
suggestion: fold the deflation into the same line, e.g. "'Fifty-one seconds,' Ruth says, 'against three guys who let you walk up to them.'" so the number and the discount arrive together

why: Ruth's examination (line 79) and her spoken report of what she found are a single continuous beat split across a paragraph break instead of joined, treating one action as two isolated events
suggestion: merge into one paragraph: "...She holds an eyelid open and looks. 'Concussion. He's fine.'"
